# netbox_module_type (Resource)

From the [official documentation](https://docs.netbox.dev/en/stable/models/dcim/moduletype/):

> A module type represents a specific make and model of hardware component which is installable within a device's module bay and has its own child components. For example, consider a chassis-based switch or router with a number of field-replaceable line cards. Each line card has its own model number and includes a certain set of components such as interfaces. Each module type may have a manufacturer, model number, and part number assigned to it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "netbox_manufacturer" "test" {
  name = "Dell"
}

resource "netbox_module_type" "test" {
  manufacturer_id = netbox_manufacturer.test.id
  model           = "Networking"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `manufacturer_id` (Number) The ID of the manufacturer associated with the module type.
- `model` (String) The model of the module type.

### Optional

- `airflow` (String) One of [front-to-rear, rear-to-front, left-to-right, right-to-left, side-to-rear, passive].
- `attributes` (String) The attributes of the module type, defined by its profile. This is best managed through the use of `jsonencode`.
- `comments` (String) Free-form comments about the module type.
- `cooling_method` (String) One of [air, liquid, hybrid, immersion]. Needs NetBox 4.7.0 or later.
- `custom_fields` (Map of String) Custom field values of the object, as a map of field name to value.
- `description` (String) A description of the module type.
- `end_of_life` (String) The date after which this module type is no longer supported by the manufacturer. Needs NetBox 4.7.0 or later.
- `module_bay_type_ids` (Set of Number) The IDs of the module bay type associated with the module type.
- `module_bay_types` (Set of Number) The IDs of the module bay types of the module type. Needs NetBox 4.7 or later.
- `owner_id` (Number) The ID of the owner associated with the module type. Needs NetBox 4.5.0 or later.
- `part_number` (String) The part number of the module type.
- `profile_id` (Number) The ID of the profile associated with the module type.
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags assigned to the object, by name.
- `weight` (Number) The weight of the module type.
- `weight_unit` (String) One of [kg, g, lb, oz]. Required when `weight` is set.

### Read-Only

- `console_port_template_count` (Number) The number of console port template objects that refer to the module type.
- `console_server_port_template_count` (Number) The number of console server port template objects that refer to the module type.
- `cooling_intake_template_count` (Number) The number of cooling intake template objects that refer to the module type.
- `cooling_outflow_template_count` (Number) The number of cooling outflow template objects that refer to the module type.
- `created` (String) When the module type was created.
- `front_port_template_count` (Number) The number of front port template objects that refer to the module type.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `interface_template_count` (Number) The number of interface template objects that refer to the module type.
- `last_updated` (String) When the module type was last changed.
- `module_bay_template_count` (Number) The number of module bay template objects that refer to the module type.
- `module_count` (Number) The number of module objects that refer to the module type.
- `power_outlet_template_count` (Number) The number of power outlet template objects that refer to the module type.
- `power_port_template_count` (Number) The number of power port template objects that refer to the module type.
- `rear_port_template_count` (Number) The number of rear port template objects that refer to the module type.
- `tags_all` (Set of String) All tags assigned to the object, including those not managed by Terraform.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The ID is the numeric NetBox ID of the object
terraform import netbox_module_type.example 1
```
